segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
they began to conquer and be conquered.
And in these times, when they gave themselves over to all manner of wantonness, debauchery, and prodigality,
more than conquering, they were conquered.
And on this account, when they wished to establish peace with the Romans,
the Romans were not willing,
but were hoping
that once again they would rule over their former dominions.
And only concerning the exchange of captives did they send envoys.
And in the year 300
300 of the Arabs,
which is the year 1224
1224 of the Greeks,
there was seen a mule that gave birth,
and many saw its foal in the land of Outer India.
And in this same year died Alexander, king of the Romans,
and after him reigned Constantine, his son,
when he was twelve years old.
And in the year 1227
(1227 of the Greeks,
916 of our Lord?), an army of the Romans went out to Tarsus,
and another army to Mar'ash.
And they took captive from the Arabs about fifty thousand souls,
and there was great mourning for the Arabs in every place.
And in this same year,
the Nestorian metropolitan of Daquqa converted to Islam in Baghdad,
and there was distress for the Christians.
And in the year 305
305 of the Arabs,
there were sent from King Constantine to the king of the Arabs two individuals as envoys,
an old man and a youth.
And when {OCR?} they arrived at Tagrit,
they made them stay there for two months, until King al-Muqtadir adorned his palace
and gathered his troops and his nobles;
and then he summoned them.
It is said
that they stationed one hundred and sixty thousand horsemen from the residence in which the envoys were lodging as far as the palace,
on both sides.
And within the outer gate they stationed five hundred horses saddled with saddles of gold and silver on one side,
and five hundred on the other side.
And in the open court within the outer residence was a multitude of harts and hinds and gazelles and fawns.
And inside the open court of the residence {OCR?}, another court, in which were four large elephants,
and on each one of them eight Indian men,
and in their hands engines of naphtha and fire.
And inside this court,
another court in which were a hundred lions,
fifty on one side
and fifty on the other side,
being bound with chains.
